structure:
A single short Markdown ruling file, 47 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-paul-2026-11-05.md), from Paul, dated 5 November 2026, on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711). It is laid out in two halves. The first half quotes Paul verbatim in six block quotes, grouped under four framing lines: on reviewing address types, roles and categories ("Role" is better terminology than "use"; proceed with the renaming and keep category out of the API for now, adding it back later if it becomes a first-class public concept; code changes to add new roles make sense); on the ticket's acceptance criteria, which still described a stored type and uses ("yes change the AC on the ticket. The correct change was made."); on the addresses saved before the change (delete the entire collection on dev and test with CDP tooling, none of the addresses has any value); and on paging the list and the pickers, which the Design Release 2.1 prototype does not page (pagination is needed else the service will struggle, even though it is missing in the prototype, and the lack of it is causing an issue in test environments where organisations have thousands of addresses). The second half is the main session's reading: eight numbered claims, each marked New, Done or a confirmation, covering the six roles and the rename, roles-only storage with no stored address type, the sending/receiving/branch grouping as an internal rule with its refusals, the list's role/searchRole parameters, adding a role in code, the ticket's own description and criteria, no migration of saved addresses, and keeping pagination with page and pageSize 1 to 100 defaulting to 25. Scope is the whole file; nothing is left out. Short enough for one agent to read every word of, so it is one part.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Part 1, "Whole ruling": the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-paul-2026-11-05.md, read in full (no other part). The file is laid out as four framing lines written by the main session, each followed by the owner's verbatim block quotes — (a) on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711), three quotes: "Role" is better terminology than "use", proceed with the renaming and keep category out of the api for now with the option to add it back later if it becomes a first class public concept, and code changes to add new roles make sense; (b) on the ticket's acceptance criteria, one quote: change the AC, the correct change was made; (c) on the addresses saved before the change, one quote: delete the entire collection on the 2 shared environments (dev, test) using CDP tooling, none of the addresses has any value; (d) on paging the list and the pickers, two quotes: pagination is needed else the service will struggle even though it is missing in the prototype, and the lack of pagination is causing an issue in test environments where organisations have 1000s of addresses. Below the quotes sit the eight numbered claims the main session read from them (1 roles on an address and the rename, 2 roles stored only and the front door's address type, 3 the sending/receiving/branch grouping and its refusals, 4 the list's role/searchRole parameters, 5 new roles added in code, 6 EUDPA-711's description and AC, 7 no migration and dropping the addresses collection, 8 pagination kept and req-611's unpaginated requirement not built). This part covers every framing line, every block quote and every numbered claim: each quote-backed decision is recorded verbatim, each numbered claim is split into one claim per fact and marked inferred where only the numbered list, not the owner's words, says it, and the points the ruling leaves open are recorded as gaps.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open when and how the grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch would be added to the API, beyond saying it is added "then" if the grouping becomes a public concept.

The ruling leaves open which of the six roles belongs to each of the sending, receiving and branch groups, although it requires each role to be in exactly one group and refuses roles from more than one group.
The ruling leaves open what happens to addresses saved before the change in any environment other than the two shared ones it names, dev and test.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open how the address pickers page: it gives parameters and limits for the list API only, and says nothing about a picker's page size or parameters.

The ruling leaves open how a role is removed or retired, and what happens to an address holding a role that is no longer offered: it covers adding a role in code only.
